text:
Nora: hey all, starting my first oncall rotation next week. can someone confirm the essentials i should complete before my shift?
Diego: welcome! key items: pager access, MFA, runbook read-throughs for your services, and staging drill shadowing.
Nora: pager and MFA done, but i'm missing access to the "payments" runbook set.
Vik: i can add you. which email did you use for SSO?
Nora: nora@redwood.ai
ops-bot: action_required: new_oncall_access_request by Nora. Please wait up to 30m for provisioning.
Diego: also, make sure you join the oncall slack channel policy thread (pinned). it lists escalation targets and sev definitions.
Nora: thanks. what's our policy for suppressing noisy alerts vs escalating?
Claire: rule of thumb: if it affects user-facing latency or errors -> escalate. if it's a duplicate/noise, annotate and confirm before muting.
Vik: for ambiguous cases, page the service owner after 15m if unresolved. we prefer early escalation.
Nora: where do i practise runbooks? any sandbox?
Diego: yes, staging runbooks live under /docs/oncall/staging-playbooks. we do shadow drills Tue/Thu 11:00. join one as observer first.
Nora: how do I hand off at end of my shift?
Claire: use /handoff in #eng-oncall and paste current list. keep it short: incidents, status, followups. example: /handoff
(Incidents: none | Notes: completed cache rotation | Followups: run compaction tomorrow)
Nora: last one: how do we request emergency help if paging chain isn't responding?
Vik: call the oncall-lead number and escalate on PagerDuty to "critical". also open a war-room and ping @exec-oncall.
ops-bot: reminder: onboarding-bootcamp session tomorrow 09:00 (invite sent).
Nora: great, i'll attend bootcamp and the Thu drill. thanks everyone!
Diego: welcome aboard and ping any of us if you want a pairing session before your first live page.
Claire: +1. i'll be oncall next week too; happy to pair on early shifts.
Nora: appreciate it :slightly_smiling_face:
